causes.text: Pfizer announced a $6.7 billion cash acquisition of Arena Pharmaceuticals, offering double its prior share price to gain the bowel-disease treatment candidate etrasimod.

source_info.title: Pfizer bets on Arena's promising bowel disease treatment in $6.7 bln deal

effects.text: Amgen said it would buy back up to $6 billion of its shares and forecast that profit could more than double by 2030. Shares jumped about 8% to $241.37.

source_info.title: Amgen to buy back $6 bln in shares this quarter, provides long-term profit forecast

causal_reasoning_chain.description: On 2021-12-13, Pfizer's $6.7 billion acquisition of Arena Pharmaceuticals signaled aggressive expansion into inflammatory bowel disease treatments, intensifying competitive pressure in immunology.
The acquisition highlighted investors' expectations that large drugmakers will deploy capital to secure future growth, prompting Amgen to demonstrate strategic flexibility.
On 2022-02-08, Amgen announced a $6 billion share buyback and long-term profit outlook to reassure shareholders. This proactive response lifted investor sentiment and the stock rose roughly 8%.

rationale: The cause reflects competitor investments that increased expectations for capital deployment. Amgen's large share repurchase and growth guidance were interpreted as a competitive response, driving the share price higher.
counterfactual_analysis: Without Pfizer's bold acquisition, investor pressure on Amgen to return cash and project long-term growth might have been milder, potentially leading to a smaller stock reaction.

adversarial_confounders.text: Positive trends in the broader biotechnology index
adversarial_confounders.impact: Sector-wide rallies may have contributed to Amgen's stock gain.

details.commentary: The sudden collapse in demand for cruises left Carnival and its peers in a brutal fight for survival, with high fixed costs and almost no revenue. As the pandemic dragged on, investors feared that those competitive and financial pressures would force deep dilutions and restructurings, justifying the severe share-price decline.
